subject: Physics

nodes.text: an object stays at rest or keeps moving at constant velocity unless a net force acts on it, a property called inertia
the acceleration of an object depends on the net force and its mass, expressed as force equals mass times acceleration
a larger mass needs a larger force to reach the same acceleration because mass resists changes in motion
for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction, so forces always come in pairs
the action and reaction forces act on two different objects, which is why they do not cancel out
it is the net (unbalanced) force that changes an object's motion

textbookPhrasings: Newton's first law states that a body continues to be in a state of rest or of uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external unbalanced force.
Newton's second law states that the rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the applied force and takes place in the direction of the force.
Newton's third law states that to every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.
referenceFacts: An object at rest stays at rest unless a net force acts on it
A larger mass requires a larger force for the same acceleration
For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction
Action and reaction forces act on different objects
A net unbalanced force is needed to change an object's motion

whyQuestions.q: Why do you lurch forward when a moving bus suddenly brakes?
whyQuestions.expectedIdea: your body's inertia keeps it moving forward even though the bus has stopped

whyQuestions.q: Why is it harder to push a loaded cart than an empty one to the same speed?
whyQuestions.expectedIdea: the loaded cart has more mass, so it needs more force for the same acceleration

whyQuestions.q: Why does a rocket move upward when it pushes gas downward?
whyQuestions.expectedIdea: the gas pushed down exerts an equal and opposite reaction force pushing the rocket up

misconceptions: A moving object will eventually stop on its own even with no force acting
Heavier objects always fall faster than lighter ones
If two objects push on each other, the bigger one pushes harder
A constant force is needed to keep an object moving at constant speed
